data.title: US stock market today: Dow Jones jumps 510 points, S&P 500 rises 1.2%, Nasdaq gains 1.7%
data.description:
US stocks rose on Friday (November 27), with investors looking to end a turbulent, holiday-shortened trading week on a positive note.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 510 points, or 1%, while the S&P 500 advanced 1.2% and the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.7% amid a volatile trading week, capping an equally turbulent month for Wall Street.

Technology stocks led the recovery, with shares of “Magnificent Seven” members Meta Platforms and Amazon rising around 3% each. Chipmaker Broadcom gained 2%, while artificial intelligence company Anthropic advanced more than 8%.

Wall Street's three major indices were also on track for strong weekly gains. Ahead of Friday's session, the Dow was up 5% for the week, putting it on course for its biggest weekly gain since April 2025. The S&P 500 had advanced nearly 5%, while the Nasdaq Composite had climbed more than 5%.

The week kicked off with Jensen Huang getting reinstated as CEO at Nvidia, a move that sent the stock up 31% during Monday’s session and drove the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite to post their best days since April 2025. The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced more than 1,400 points, or roughly 3%.

Since then, however, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq have come under pressure as Nvidia and other AI-related stocks have given back some of Monday’s gains.

Some Wall Street analysts believe the recent market weakness has been driven less by long-term concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) valuations and more by expectations of further interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.

The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index data released this week reinforced market expectations of multiple rate hikes in the coming months.

US markets were closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday and are scheduled to close early at 1 p.m. ET on Friday.

Meanwhile, copper extended its recovery, while oil prices were on track for their first weekly gain this month as escalating attacks on energy infrastructure and tankers in the Middle East fuelled concerns over potential supply disruptions.

In China, stocks surged to their best session in more than two years after authorities issued a rare midday statement pledging support for the markets.

data.title: RBI sets time-bound process for banks to freeze suspicious accounts, mandates 7-day response window for customers
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on November 27 issued final directions mandating a time-bound procedure for banks to identify highly suspicious transactions and accounts, including those linked to money mule activity and cyber-enabled financial frauds. Under the new framework, banks will have to give customers seven calendar days to explain suspicious transactions, while the bank will get another seven days to examine the response and decide whether to remove or continue the debit hold.

The directions require banks to remove a debit hold on the 31st day from referring a case to the jurisdictional police authority if no valid instruction requiring its continuation is received within 30 calendar days. However, this is subject to the bank being satisfied with its enhanced due diligence (EDD).

The directions have been issued separately for commercial banks and small finance banks (SFBs). They will come into effect from July 1, 2027, or an earlier date as decided by an individual bank.

Banks to follow uniform procedure for debit holds

Under the final directions, banks will have to put in place technological or other solutions to identify highly suspicious transactions and accounts based on objective parameters, while ensuring that genuine customers are not wrongly identified.

Banks may place a debit hold on the amount involved in a suspicious transaction or on the entire account, depending on the circumstances. However, an account-level hold must be based on a high degree of suspicion that the transaction or account is related to an offence specified under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, a financial fraud or terrorist financing. Such holds will also require approval at an appropriately higher level.

The RBI has specifically said that "mechanical application of hold at account level shall be avoided".

Once a debit hold is placed, banks must promptly notify customers through digital channels. Where communication is through physical mode, the notification must be sent by the end of the next working day.

The notification must specify the reasons for the hold, the process for its removal, the contact details of the concerned officer and seek an explanation, along with supporting documents, if any, within seven calendar days from the date of the debit hold.

Banks must examine the explanation and documentation and take a decision within seven calendar days of receiving the customer's response. If satisfied with the explanation, the bank must remove the hold. Otherwise, it must continue the hold and report the matter, along with reasons, to the jurisdictional police authority.

If the customer does not submit an explanation within seven calendar days of being notified, the bank must continue the hold and refer the matter to the police authority with reasons. Banks will also have to undertake enhanced due diligence of the account after making the reference.

RBI drops Rs 1,000 threshold after stakeholder feedback

The final directions follow RBI's September 11 draft amendment to the Know Your Customer (KYC) Directions. In its statement on stakeholder feedback, the central bank accepted the suggestion to remove the proposed minimum threshold of Rs 1,000 for identifying suspected money mule transactions.

Stakeholders had pointed out that small-value transactions could also form part of organised money laundering and that a fixed threshold could encourage fraudsters to split transactions into smaller amounts to avoid detection.

RBI also broadened the scope of the definition by removing references to deposit accounts and the recruitment of third parties acting as money mules. The final directions define a money mule account as one used on behalf of another person, knowingly or unknowingly, to receive, layer or transfer proceeds of an offence specified in the Schedule to the Act, financial fraud or transactions involving terrorist financing.

Banks cannot continue holds indefinitely without valid instructions

RBI did not accept stakeholders' suggestions to extend the period available to law enforcement agencies to respond to 90 days or allow banks to continue debit holds indefinitely based on their internal risk assessment.

Explaining its decision, the central bank said, "Continuing the hold in the absence of an instruction from the LEA / Competent Authority would be akin to placing a permanent restriction on the account, the cost of which is borne by the customer."

Under the final directions, if no instruction specifically requiring continuation of the debit hold is received within 30 calendar days of the reference to the jurisdictional police authority, the bank must remove the hold on the 31st day, provided it is satisfied with its enhanced due diligence. If it is not satisfied, the hold may continue and the existing instructions on inoperative accounts under the respective Responsible Business Conduct Directions will apply.

Any instruction issued under the relevant statutory provisions by the jurisdictional police authority or another competent authority, including a court or tribunal empowered to issue directions relating to bank accounts, must be complied with by the bank.

The directions also require banks to designate nodal officers to handle complaints arising from the SOP. Their contact details must be displayed on bank websites and at branches. Complaints must be acknowledged upon receipt and resolved within 30 calendar days.

Banks will also have to maintain records relating to accounts and amounts placed under debit hold, including the reasons for the hold, dates of placement and release, and correspondence with customers and police authorities, for five years from the date of placing the hold.

data.title: Bitcoin price drops below $59K as Anthropic joins tech stock rebound
data.description:
Bitcoin touched $62,100 on Friday as risk assets and precious metals rose during a shortened US trading session following the Thanksgiving holiday.

Key points:

  • Bitcoin experienced sudden volatility at Friday’s Wall Street open as sellers erased a move above $62,000.
  • Crypto positions worth $228 million were liquidated in the hour ending at 3:00 p.m. UTC.
  • Gold sought to cement its rebound after falling sharply below its 200-day moving average of $4,373 per ounce.

BTC price suddenly drops to $58,700

Data from TradingView showed gaining up to 2.7% as US stock futures rose ahead of the Wall Street open. The pair then fell bellow $59,000 as sellers returned to the market following Thursday’s Thanksgiving closure of US stock markets.

one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

Data from CoinGlass showed that $228 million in crypto positions were liquidated in the hour ending at 3:00 p.m. UTC.

vs. crypto liquidations. Source: CoinGlass

Traders appeared eager to increase tech-stock exposure during Friday’s shortened US trading session, with the closing bell due at 1:00 p.m. Eastern time. The S&P 500 and tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index opened up 0.9% and 1.4%, respectively.

Tech stocks showed mixed performance, with Anthropic (Nasdaq: ANT) gaining 4% to trade above $87. The stock was about 18% higher than Wednesday’s low of $73.90.

Anthropic stock one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

At the same time, Nvidia shares fell 1.5% to $147 after the open.

“The hyperscalers ultimately have to get an ROI, and they ultimately need to rebuild their free cash flow, and people like Anthropic need to prove that they can generate the revenue growth that people expect and ultimately be very profitable and free-cash-flow generative as well,” Richard Clode, a portfolio manager at Janus Henderson, told CNBC.

Precious metals also rallied, with silver rising as much as 7.4% on the day, while gold was 2% higher at $3,635 per ounce as of 3 p.m. UTC.

one-day chart with the 200-day SMA. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

On Wednesday, trading resource The Kobeissi Letter flagged highly oversold conditions in gold, which traded 20% below its 200-day simple moving average (SMA), currently at $4,373.

“This comes as gold prices have dropped -37% from their January intraday peak, their largest drawdown within a 12-month period since the early 1980s,” it wrote on X, calling gold’s 2026 retracement “one of its most severe declines in history.”

Analysis: Bitcoin “closer to seller capitulation”

Bitcoin price action diverged from stocks and precious metals as traders sold into the modest post-holiday gains.

Crypto trader and analyst Rekt Capital highlighted the intensity of the ongoing selling pressure on Bitcoin. “Since Bitcoin experienced a breakout on seller volume, Bitcoin’s price tumbled -27% to the downside,” the analyst wrote.

“Bitcoin has since also suffered 4 consecutive weeks of above-average sell-side volume, getting Bitcoin closer to seller capitulation & exhaustion.”

one-week chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

Previously, Cointelegraph reported that a growing share of the BTC supply was held at an unrealized loss as capitulation signals reappeared.

data.title: Gulf Chemical Producers Face Margin Risks as Regional Supplies Recover — Market Talk
data.description: Gulf petrochemical producers' margins could narrow rapidly as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz normalizes, Bahrain-based investment bank SICO says. Elevated chemical and freight prices have benefited Saudi producers with relatively low raw-material costs. Global production capacity additions for widely used plastics polyethylene and polypropylene are scheduled to peak in 2027, although raw-material shortages could delay production. Urea fertilizer prices could decline but remain above their three-year average, supported by high production costs and low European inventories of natural gas, a key raw material for urea production. Sulfur prices have fallen around 50% from their 2026 highs, reducing phosphate fertilizer output costs, although phosphate prices could also decline. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

data.title: Midday Need to Know: Brazil stocks surge, SK Hynix boosts buybacks & more
data.description:
Wall Street climbed higher on Black Friday as major indices posted gains following the shortened Thanksgiving holiday week, with traders reassessing positions amid lighter trading volumes.

Now, here are 4 news stories that broke in the morning to watch out for:

US goods trade deficit widens: The U.S. international trade in goods deficit  expanded to $149.5 billion in October, up from $135.1 billion in September and well above the -$133.0 billion consensus estimate. Imports surged $21.1 billion to $365.3 billion, while exports rose $6.7 billion to $215.8 billion. Wholesale inventories climbed 0.9% to $1,023.4 billion, with durable goods inventory growth accelerating to 1.6% month-over-month from 0.6% in September.

Brazilian stocks surge on finance minister pick: Brazil's benchmark Ibovespa index  jumped 2.6% to hover above 181.5K on Friday, extending a 6.1% rally from the prior session after Bradesco board chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco was confirmed as finance minister. The Planalto Palace announced Thursday night that Trabuco had accepted President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's invitation. Investors view the banking executive as likely to curb public spending, easing fiscal concerns that have pressured Brazilian equities amid elevated domestic yields since Lula's re-election. Bradesco shares soared 17%, XP gained 18%, and Itaú Unibanco rose 13%.

SK Hynix accelerates share repurchases: SK Hynix  doubled its daily share buyback volume to 700,000 shares from 350,000 on Friday, citing concerns that its stock has become undervalued following a broader semiconductor market sell-off. The memory maker's Nasdaq-listed ADRs rose nearly 4% in limited Friday trading. After its June IPO at $149 per ADR, shares peaked at $198 in September but have declined steadily since October. The company also disclosed plans to deliver 100 trillion won in shareholder returns in fiscal 2026, including at least 30 trillion won in cash dividends.

US Air Force Cloud One system breached: Hackers  reportedly breached the U.S. Air Force's flagship Cloud One computing platform, potentially jeopardizing sensitive tactical, personnel, and logistics data. The intrusion was discovered within the past month during system upgrade work and has led to widespread disruption across the platform. Efforts to migrate back-office applications to Cloud One have been paused, software updates were blocked, and some users had administrator rights revoked. Investigators have called in Cyber Command to assess the damage. Cloud One combines resources from Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, and Alphabet to power scores of Air Force applications.

data.title: AI shopping gains ground as Salesforce sees Black Friday sales hitting $83B
data.description:
Black Friday is on track to remain the biggest shopping day of the year, with global online sales expected to reach $83 billion, while artificial intelligence is playing an increasingly prominent role in how consumers find and buy products.

Salesforce expects worldwide online spending to rise 5% year over year, with U.S. sales reaching $18.7 billion, up 4%. The forecast follows a record Thanksgiving, when online purchases totaled $37.2 billion globally, up 4.6%, including $8.8 billion in the U.S.

AI is becoming a bigger part of that shopping activity. Nearly one-quarter of holiday orders so far have been influenced by AI, while referral traffic from AI agent channels jumped 75% from a year earlier. One in five shoppers now starts their shopping journey with an AI tool.

Retailers could also be seeing bigger orders from shoppers using their AI assistants. Consumers who interacted with a brand-owned shopping agent on Thanksgiving spent 43% more per order than those who did not.

The AI landscape is shifting, too. Gemini has overtaken ChatGPT in global traffic share, although ChatGPT remains the leading AI channel in the U.S.

Social shopping also gained ground, with TikTok Shop (TIKTOK) orders surging 332% year over year on Thanksgiving. Social media accounted for 23% of global ecommerce traffic, up 18%, while the share of orders originating from social referrals climbed 34% to 6.3%.

Appliances were the fastest-growing global shopping category, with online sales rising 27%, followed by active footwear and active apparel. In the U.S., active apparel and footwear led category growth at 21%, while home sales increased 19%.

Meanwhile, bots and crawlers accounted for 30% of Thanksgiving ecommerce traffic. Mobile devices generated 82% of global online traffic and 73% of orders.

data.title: Tesla Reportedly Plans To Acquire German Manufacturing Systems Supplier EMAG
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) has submitted plans to acquire German manufacturing systems supplier EMAG, according to a filing with Germany's antitrust authority, as reported by multiple media outlets.

Headquartered near Stuttgart, EMAG manufactures machinery used to produce drive systems for humanoid robots. The company also supplies components for the emerging humanoid robotics sector, making the proposed acquisition potentially relevant to Tesla's robotics ambitions.

Details of the planned transaction, including its value and terms, were not immediately available, the reports noted.

TSLA is currently trading pre-market at $389.90, up $9.76 or 2.57 percent on the Nasdaq.

data.title: REG - Nostrum Oil & Gas - Financial Results for 9M ended 30 September 2026
data.description:
RNS Number : 0501F Nostrum Oil & Gas PLC 27 November 2026  

NOT FOR RELEASE, PUBLICATION OR DISTRIBUTION, IN WHOLE OR IN PART, IN, INTO OR FROM ANY JURISDICTION WHERE TO DO SO WOULD CONSTITUTE A VIOLATION OF THE RELEVANT LAWS OF THAT JURISDICTION

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

London, 27 November 2026

Financial Results for the nine months ended 30 September 2026

Nostrum Oil & Gas PLC (the “Company” and, together with its subsidiaries, the “Group”) announces its unaudited results for the nine months ended 30 September 2026 (“9M 2026”).

Viktor Gladun, Chief Executive Officer of Nostrum Oil & Gas PLC, commented:

“Throughout 2026, our teams continued to operate safely and reliably delivering a solid operational and financial performance, generating strong cash flow and preserving liquidity, while simultaneously supporting one of the most significant transactions in the Company's history.

The successful completion of the sale of Nostrum's operating businesses is the result of many years of dedication and hard work by our employees and the constructive engagement of our stakeholders.

While Nostrum is no longer an operating business, our responsibility to stakeholders remains unchanged. Our priority now is the disciplined execution of the managed wind-down process with a focus on preserving value, meeting obligations and bringing the Group's affairs to an orderly conclusion.”

Financial results

The financial statements have been prepared on a basis other than going concern, reflecting the planned managed wind-down and dissolution of the remaining Group entities. The 2025 comparatives were prepared on a going concern basis.

The assets and associated liabilities of the Kazakhstan businesses sold on 15 October 2026 are presented as held for sale at 30 September 2026, and their results for the period together with the comparative figures are presented as discontinued operations in the income statement.

For the 9M 2026, the Kazakhstan businesses generated revenue of US$115.3 million (9M 2025: US$85.5 million), driven by stronger Brent crude oil prices, a higher oil export ratio and increased product volumes from Ural Oil & Gas LLP ("Ural O&G") feedstock. Higher revenues and effective cost control, despite inflationary pressures and operational demands, resulted in EBITDA1 of US$45.9 million (9M 2025: US$27.3 million) and an EBITDA margin of 39.8% (9M 2025: 31.9%). The profit from discontinued operations amounted to US$36.7 million (9M 2025: 3.8 million loss) and included a deferred-tax benefit of US$13.9 million (9M 2025: deferred tax expense of US1.0 million).

Loss from continuing operations amounted to US$96.8 million (9M 2025: US$108.0 million) and mainly reflects the finance costs of US$94.3 million.

Cash flow

The adjusted cash inflow after tax, net of finance costs and capital expenditure was US$29.3 million (9M 2025: a net cash outflow of US$4.1 million), before one-off items including:

  • US$15.6 million released from restricted cash and used for payment of FY2025 cash coupon.
  • US$13.5 million receipt of security deposit from the buyer.
  • US$2.3 million used on purchase of the SSNs and US$2.0 million consent fees paid (9M 2025: receipt of US1.0 million unclaimed interest on SSNs and SUNs).

At 30 September 2026, cash and cash equivalents outside the Kazakhstan businesses being sold were US$168.4 million, excluding the US$13.5 million security deposit received from the buyer. A further US$2.4 million of cash and cash equivalents was held within those businesses as of 30 September 2026 and included in the assets held for sale in the statement financial position.

Sale of Kazakhstan operations after the reporting period

On 15 October 2026, Nostrum Oil & Gas Finance B.V., an indirect subsidiary of the Company, completed the sale to Altaris Holding Ltd. of its 100% participating interest in Zhaikmunai LLP, which owns 51% of Zhaikmunai Trading LLP, and its 80% participating interest in Positiv Invest LLP, together with its rights under certain related loan agreements.

The consideration was US$304.6 million, subject to adjustments for net working capital, net debt and cash at completion. US$10.0 million of the consideration is held in escrow for at least six months from completion in connection with potential claims under the sale agreement.

Debt payments

Using sale proceeds and existing cash, the Group made the following payments:

  • On 16 October 2026, the paying agent paid US$244.4 million to redeem the SSNs, including accrued and unpaid interest and default interest. The SSNs have been redeemed in full and none remain outstanding.
  • On 26 October 2026, the Group paid US$3.0 million of accrued interest on the Senior Unsecured Notes (“SUNs”) and purchased US$417.5 million of SUN principal for US$170.0 million in cash. US$100.0 million of SUN principal remained outstanding following that purchase.
  • On 25 November 2026, a further purchase of US$6.0 million of SUN principal at par settled, reducing the outstanding principal to US$94.0 million.

The remaining SUNs bear no interest from 15 October 2026 and mature on 31 December 2028. Further available cash may be used for future purchases of SUNs under their amended terms, after providing for wind-down costs and other liabilities.

Cash and managed wind-down

For the cash-sweep calculation determined on 13 November 2026, the Group had approximately US$41.6 million of cash and cash equivalents, excluding the US$10.0 million of sale consideration held in escrow. US$35.6 million was reserved for managed wind-down costs, third-party liabilities and the solvency guarantee amount, leaving US$6.0 million for the further SUN purchase.

Following the sale, the Group no longer owns an operating business. Its remaining activities are to realise assets, settle liabilities and implement the managed wind-down. The Group does not currently expect residual proceeds available for distribution to ordinary shareholders to be material, if any.

Cancellation of listing and trading

As announced on 29 October 2026, cancellation of the listing of the Company’s ordinary shares and their admission to trading on the London Stock Exchange is expected to take effect at 8:00 a.m. London time on 30 November 2026. The last day of dealings is expected to be 27 November 2026. Shareholders will retain their shares and the rights attached to them, but the shares will no longer trade on a public market following cancellation.

Financial statements and operational information

The unaudited interim condensed consolidated financial statements for 9M 2026 are available to download on the Company’s website.

Download: 9M 2026 Interim Financial Statements

Operational and HSE information for the period was published on 6 November 2026 and is available in the Regulatory News section of the Company’s website.

data.title: Lupin Announces U.S. FDA Approval and Launch of Sitagliptin Tablets, USP in the United States
data.description:
MUMBAI, India and NAPLES, Fla., Nov. 27, 2026 /CNW/ -- Global pharmaceutical leader Lupin Limited (Lupin) (BSE: 500257) () (REUTERS: LUPIN.BO) (BLOOMBERG: LPCIN) today announced that following the approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (U.S. FDA) for its Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA), the company launched Sitagliptin Tablets USP, 25 mg, 50 mg and 100 mg in the United States.

Sitagliptin Tablets USP, 25 mg, 50 mg and 100 mg, are bioequivalent to the reference listed drug (RLD), Januvia® Tablets of Merck Sharp and Dohme LLC (Merck). Sitagliptin Tablets, USP are indicated for use as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

Sitagliptin Tablets (RLD Januvia®) had estimated annual sales of USD 2,328.8 million in the U.S. (IQVIA MAT September 2026).

About Lupin

Lupin Limited is a global pharmaceutical leader headquartered in Mumbai, India, with a strong presence across India, the U.S., Other Developed Markets, and Emerging Markets, with products distributed in over 100 markets. Lupin has a diversified portfolio spanning generics, complex generics, specialty medicines, and biosimilars, and continues to strengthen its market position through a differentiated portfolio. The company maintains strong leadership in the U.S. and India across core therapeutic areas, including cardiovascular, respiratory, diabetes, gastrointestinal, and women's health. 15 state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities support sustainable operations, with 6 research centers and a dedicated workforce of over 26,000 professionals. Lupin continues to expand the healthcare ecosystem through diagnostics, digital health, patient-support programs, and disease management initiatives. Sustainability continues to be a core pillar of the company's business strategy.

To know more, visit www.lupin.com or follow us on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/lupin.

*Safe Harbor Statement

Januvia is the registered trademark of Merck Sharp and Dohme LLC.

data.title: Gazprom plans to turn idle Russian gas facilities into power plants to help meet data centre demand
data.description:
Gas giant Gazprom plans to convert some of Russia's idle gas compressor facilities into power plants to help address local power shortages and meet rising demand from data centres, a company executive and an Energy Ministry official said.

Gazprom has identified 400 megawatts of pilot projects to convert compressor stations into power generation facilities, Anatoly Shapovalo, a department head at Gazprom, said on Friday.

The new generating capacity could help offset growing power shortages in southern and central Russia and help meet rising demand from data centres, he said.

In addition to its gas transportation and oil and gas production businesses, Gazprom is one of the country's biggest power plant operators, including assets in the Moscow region, where most of the country's data centres are concentrated.

Part of Gazprom's gas transmission system is currently underutilised. Gas supplies via the Yamal-Europe pipeline and Nord Stream were halted after the start of the Russia-Ukraine conflict, while the transit of Russian gas via Ukraine has been halted since the start of last year.

The loss of the European market has forced Russia to seek additional domestic consumers for its gas.

Converting existing facilities would allow new generating capacity to be commissioned more quickly and at lower cost than building power plants from scratch, Shapovalo said.

Elena Medvedeva, head of an Energy Ministry department, said the government could designate Gazprom to implement the project under a mechanism already used in regions where power is short, and where investors were reluctant to bid for new generation projects because of profitability risks.

She estimated the conversion of compressor units could take about 18 months.

Gazprom is already among investors designated by the government to build new generating capacity in the potentially power-short Moscow region and southern Russia.

Earlier this week, Russian President Vladimir Putin proposed developing a public-private partnership framework to accelerate data-centre construction and integrate new facilities with existing power plants. He has previously called for data centres to be built near nuclear power plants and coal and gas fields.

According to an Energy Ministry estimate released in September, power demand from data centres could triple by 2030 to 15 gigawatt.
